registry: The Tank Guide University Research Library

verification_status.verified: Source located at its official location; citation metadata as registered is correct and the content supports the use described in verification_note.
verification_status.verified_with_metadata_correction: Source located and content verified, but registered citation metadata (title, author, publisher, year, DOI, or canonical URL) required correction.
verification_status.verified_limited_scope: Source located and verified, but it supports only a narrower scope than the package use implies.
verification_status.broken_or_moved: Registered URL no longer resolves to the cited source and no verified replacement location has been recorded.
verification_status.citation_problem: Citation metadata could not be reconciled with the source located (wrong title, author, or document).
verification_status.unable_to_verify: Source could not be located or checked during verification.
verification_status.unverified_citation_from_package: Legacy pre-verification status: citation metadata recorded as given in the package and not yet checked against the live source. No longer assigned to any Summer Heat pilot record.

evidence_role.reference_data: Source of specific numeric values or relationships used by the package.
evidence_role.applied_guidance: Extension/aquaculture applied guidance; context differs from home aquariums.
evidence_role.preparedness_and_safety_guidance: General emergency-preparedness or safety guidance; not aquarium-specific.
evidence_role.preparedness_context: Contextual background for severe-weather preparedness; not aquarium-specific.
evidence_role.analogous_guidance_limited_scope: Non-aquarium guidance used only for a narrowly stated principle.
evidence_role.manufacturer_product_documentation: Vendor documentation of its own product features. Not independent scientific evidence.

source_origin.original_package_citation: Cited in the original research package's bibliography (carries an original_package_key such as S1–S16).
source_origin.supplementary_verification_source: Added later during an independent verification pass to support a claim whose original citation was mismatched. Not an original package citation; carries no original_package_key.

sources.title: Chapter A6.2. Dissolved oxygen
sources.publication_or_publisher: U.S. Geological Survey — Techniques and Methods 9-A6.2
sources.package_description: Table 6.2-2 provides freshwater oxygen solubility by temperature and atmospheric pressure.
sources.verification_note: This is the revised October 2020 USGS National Field Manual chapter. It supports dissolved-oxygen solubility/reference data and temperature-related oxygen-solubility calculations. It does not directly establish aquarium cooling by evaporation from a fan.
notes: [Registration note; superseded by the independent verification pass] Year not stated in the package.
Package uses Table 6.2-2 values at 760 mm Hg (8.42 mg/L at 24°C, 7.56 mg/L at 30°C) and is the stated source for Figure 1 and the tropical-tank table.

Package also cites S1 as research basis for the fan/evaporative-cooling subsection; the package's own description of S1 covers oxygen solubility only, so that relationship is recorded as cited but flagged for review in source-usage.json.
Title as registered from the package: 'Chapter A6.2, Dissolved Oxygen, National Field Manual for the Collection of Water-Quality Data'.
Series: Techniques and Methods 9-A6.2 (USGS National Field Manual for the Collection of Water-Quality Data). Revised October 2020.
Alternate/archive URL (direct PDF, as registered from the package): https://pubs.usgs.gov/tm/09/a6.2/tm9a6.2.pdf

Verification pass: S1 does not support the package's evaporative-fan-cooling claim (USE-summer-heat-014 marked unsupported_or_mismatched; replacement source needed). The historical citation is preserved.

Fan-cooling gap resolved: USE-summer-heat-014 remains unsupported_or_mismatched as a historical citation; the claim now has supplementary support from SRC-usgs-evaporation-water-surfaces-1898 and SRC-usgs-evaporation-water-cycle-2019.

sources.title: Dissolved Oxygen and Water
sources.package_description: Explains that cold water can hold more dissolved oxygen than warm water.
sources.verification_note: Directly supports the principle that cold water can hold more dissolved oxygen than warm water. It is explanatory USGS material, not a peer-reviewed study.
notes: [Registration note; superseded by the independent verification pass] Year not stated in the package. Web page; publication/update date not recorded.
Current page date: August 24, 2026.
Author/organization corrected from 'U.S. Geological Survey' to 'Water Science School'; publisher is U.S. Geological Survey.

sources.title: CADDIS: Dissolved Oxygen
sources.package_description: Describes atmospheric oxygen absorption, enhancement by turbulence, and high-temperature reduction in oxygen solubility.
sources.verification_note: The EPA page directly states that atmospheric oxygen absorption is enhanced by turbulence, that high temperature reduces oxygen solubility, and lists biological signs associated with low dissolved oxygen such as fish gulping air. It does not directly support evaporative cooling from blowing a fan across an aquarium.
notes: Year not stated in the package. Web page; publication/update date not recorded.
Package also relies on this source for 'fish gulping air' as a biological effect associated with low dissolved oxygen (Section 4).

Verification pass: S3 does not support the package's evaporative-fan-cooling claim (USE-summer-heat-015 marked unsupported_or_mismatched; replacement source needed). The historical citation is preserved.

Fan-cooling gap resolved: USE-summer-heat-015 remains unsupported_or_mismatched as a historical citation; the claim now has supplementary support from SRC-usgs-evaporation-water-surfaces-1898 and SRC-usgs-evaporation-water-cycle-2019.

sources.title: The effects of temperature on aerobic metabolism: towards a mechanistic understanding of the responses of ectotherms to a changing environment
sources.package_description: Peer-reviewed review describing temperature-metabolism relationships and thermal performance.
sources.verification_note: This is a peer-reviewed review. It supports the general relationship between environmental temperature and aerobic metabolic rate in ectotherms. It is broader than ornamental aquarium fish and should retain that scope limitation.
notes: [Registration note; superseded by the independent verification pass] DOI not given in the package; URL is a PubMed record, not the publisher page.
[Registration note; superseded by the independent verification pass] Volume, issue, and pages not given in the package.

Package uses this source to support 'aerobic metabolic rate generally rises with temperature and then can decline at higher temperatures' and explicitly rejects a universal 'metabolism doubles' claim.
Title as registered from the package: 'The effects of temperature on aerobic metabolism'.
Journal of Experimental Biology, volume 218, issue/part 12, pages 1856–1866 (2015).
Alternate reference URL (PubMed record, as registered from the package): https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26085663/
Scope limitation: ectotherms generally; broader than ornamental aquarium fish.

sources.title: Dissolved Oxygen for Fish Production
sources.package_description: Discusses warm water holding less oxygen and increasing fish physiological oxygen demand.
sources.verification_note: This source directly states both sides of the Summer Heat “thermal oxygen squeeze”: warm water holds less dissolved oxygen, while higher water temperatures increase fish metabolic rate and physiological oxygen demand.
notes: [Registration note; superseded by the independent verification pass] Year and authors not stated in the package.
Aquaculture/fish-production context; package limitations note that home aquariums are smaller systems and application should remain cautious.
Publication identifier: FA27 / FA002.
Year field records the current supported-version release year (2021). Original publication year: 1992. Reviewed: 2024.
Author/organization corrected from 'University of Florida IFAS Extension' to author Ruth Francis-Floyd; publisher UF/IFAS Extension.

sources.title: Aeration of Ponds Used in Aquaculture
sources.author_or_organization: Perry L. Oakes; Kale Gullett; Todd Bobowick
sources.package_description: Describes diffusion, turbulence, and physical agitation of surface water as mechanisms of atmospheric oxygen transfer.
sources.verification_note: The source directly explains that atmospheric oxygen enters water through diffusion or turbulence from physical surface agitation, and that mechanical agitation, bubbling and splashing increase oxygen transfer. This is aquaculture guidance and must not be presented as a home-aquarium experiment.
notes: [Registration note; superseded by the independent verification pass] Package attributes the document jointly to USDA-NRCS and UAPB; classified as government because the package text and file name identify it as NRCS guidance (NRCS-AEN-3). University co-attribution retained; needs verification.
[Registration note; superseded by the independent verification pass] Year and authors not stated in the package. The '2023/07' in the URL is the host upload path, not a confirmed publication date.
Pond aquaculture context; package cautions that home-aquarium application should remain cautious.
Document: Agricultural Engineering Technical Note No. AEN-3 (USDA NRCS, 2011).
The University of Arkansas at Pine Bluff is the current file host only, not the author or publisher. No more canonical NRCS URL is present in the registry, so the UAPB-hosted PDF URL is retained.

sources.title: CADDIS: Ammonia
sources.package_description: Explains ammonia forms, the more toxic un-ionized NH3 form, and effects of pH and temperature.
sources.verification_note: The EPA page states that unionized versus ionized ammonia must be evaluated with temperature and pH, that the unionized fraction rises with pH, and that temperature affects ammonia toxicity. It also documents breathing-related physiological/behavioral effects that can overlap with other aquarium stress signs.
notes: Year not stated in the package. Web page; publication/update date not recorded.

sources.title: Aquatic Life Ambient Water Quality Criteria for Ammonia – Freshwater 2013
sources.publication_or_publisher: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, Office of Water / Office of Science and Technology
sources.package_description: Includes ammonia speciation relationships, pH effects, and temperature equation.
sources.verification_note: The document explicitly provides the freshwater equations for calculating NH3/NH4+ fractions using pH and temperature. It directly supports the package's ammonia-speciation calculation. The package-generated table remains a derived calculation, not a table copied from EPA.
notes: Year 2013 is taken from the document title as given in the package.
Package uses this source for the '~tenfold per pH unit, ~twofold per 10°C (0–30°C)' relationship and as the basis for its own calculated Figure 2 NH3-fraction table.
Package caveat: the Figure 2 table is 'a chemistry illustration, not a safe-exposure chart.'
Publisher detail: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, Office of Water / Office of Science and Technology.

sources.title: Water Quality Considerations for Aquaculture
sources.author_or_organization: Robert C. Summerfelt (Department of Animal Ecology, Iowa State University, Ames, Iowa)
sources.publication_or_publisher: File hosted by Ohio State University South Centers (host only; not the author or publisher)
sources.package_description: Notes increased fish oxygen consumption after feeding and other drivers of oxygen demand.
sources.verification_note: The document directly states that fish respiratory rate increases with increasing temperature and following feeding, and that oxygen consumption increases after feeding. It therefore supports those physiological mechanisms. Translating that mechanism into “feed lighter during extreme aquarium heat” remains practical husbandry inference rather than a direct tested aquarium prescription.
notes: [Registration note; superseded by the independent verification pass] Package attribution is itself hedged ('Ohio State University / aquaculture water-quality guidance'); authorship and original publisher need verification.

[Registration note; superseded by the independent verification pass] Classified university_extension because the package calls it 'Ohio State aquaculture guidance' hosted on an OSU South Centers site; needs verification.

Ohio State University South Centers is only the current PDF file host. This is not an Ohio State University Extension publication.

sources.title: Guidelines for the Use of Fishes in Research
sources.author_or_organization: Use of Fishes in Research Committee (American Fisheries Society, American Institute of Fishery Research Biologists, American Society of Ichthyologists and Herpetologists)
sources.package_description: States sufficient aeration can be supplied by compressed air, oxygen, or agitation.
sources.verification_note: The guideline states that sufficient aeration may be supplied by compressed air, injected/bottled oxygen, or agitation; it also discusses backup generators and backup power in aquatic systems. It directly supports the life-support principle, while hobby-specific battery-air-pump advice remains a practical translation.
notes: [Registration note; superseded by the independent verification pass] URL is a third-party institutional copy (UCSB IACUC), not the publishing societies' own site.

sources.package_description: General outage preparation and generator safety guidance.
sources.verification_note: Current official Ready.gov power-outage material advises using generators outdoors at least 20 feet from building openings, gathering supplies ahead of severe weather, keeping electronics charged, and planning alternate power. This is general household emergency guidance rather than aquarium-specific evidence.
notes: Year not stated in the package. Web page; publication/update date not recorded.

sources.package_description: Notes Atlantic hurricane season timing and severe-weather preparedness context.

This supports general storm preparedness. Turning that into an aquarium-specific emergency kit is a practical translation.
notes: Year not stated in the package. Web page; publication/update date not recorded.

sources.title: Instructions for measuring the rate of evaporation from water surfaces
sources.author_or_organization: Water Resources Division, U.S. Geological Survey
sources.verification_note: USGS states that evaporation from water surfaces varies with water temperature, dryness of the air, and velocity of the wind at the water surface.
notes: SUPPLEMENTARY VERIFICATION SOURCE: not cited in the original research package and not part of the S1–S16 bibliography. Added during the independent verification pass to resolve the evaporative-fan-cooling source gap (USE-summer-heat-014, USE-summer-heat-015).
This is not aquarium-specific research.
Its value to the Summer Heat package is the physical principle that increased air movement across an exposed water surface can increase evaporation.

sources.title: Evaporation and the Water Cycle
sources.verification_note: USGS explains that evaporation requires energy and removes heat from the environment, producing net cooling. The page also describes evaporative cooling systems in which a fan moves air across wet material and causes water to evaporate, and notes that evaporation is used to cool heated water in cooling-tower applications.
notes: SUPPLEMENTARY VERIFICATION SOURCE: not cited in the original research package and not part of the S1–S16 bibliography. Added during the independent verification pass to resolve the evaporative-fan-cooling source gap (USE-summer-heat-014, USE-summer-heat-015).
This is not an aquarium-specific experiment.
